eligibility.evidence: Method pp7-10: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o give relatedness and judgment-of-learning ratings for garden-path sentence pairs (cites Nelson 1990, Koriat 1997); same task run on 78 Prolific participants; new model and human data.

A.title: Judgments of learning distinguish humans from large language models in predicting memory

paradigms.name: Judgment of learning (memorability rating of a garden-path sentence after a fitting or unfitting context sentence) predicting human recognition memory

D.population: English-speaking adults recruited via Prolific, mean age 46.04
D.metric: slope of recognition accuracy on JOL (bootstrapped mixed model, 95% CI)

effects.es_metric: bootstrapped slope of human recognition on JOL, fitting context (95% CI model [-0.147, 0.172]; human [0.018, 0.316])

E.headline: Human judgments of learning predict item-level recognition memory; none of the three GPT models' ratings do, in either context.

G.notes: Conclusion rests on non-significant model slopes (CIs include zero) set beside a significant human slope; no direct test of the model-human slope difference. Human learning phase used 22 pairs per person, models rated all 45. Zero-shot single prompt wording. Query dates not given.
